title: Voice-layer announcer claims the Marine Band recording is over a hundred years old
description:
## Observed
The announcer in `examples/voice-layer.apr` (`samples/voice/announcer.wav`, made with macOS `say`) says: "Ladies and gentlemen, the United States Marine Band, **recorded more than a hundred years ago**. Chopped. Looped. And played again. Listen closely. Every sound gets a second life."

## Why it's wrong
The Thunderer source is the Marine Band's **2017** recording (`samples/sources.json`: `recorded: 2017`, `composed: 1889`). The march is old; the recording is not.

## Fix
Regenerate the line with Auritus (kokoro): "…the United States Marine Band, playing a march written more than a century ago. …". Keep the same 8 phrases, because the score's `words` and `fast` kits index them (4 "Chopped.", 5 "Looped.", 6 "And played again.", 8 the last line). Re-analyze the manifest, update the example and design comments that say it was made with `say`, and then move the persistent library and S3 copy over (the S3 push needs the user's OK). Record the script, so the words are no longer only inside an audio file.
